## When to use it

**In Dense data:** A fixed-length one-time code sent by text or email. Not for passwords or any other value.

- **Use it when:** A short code sent by text or email, typed or pasted.
- **Not when:** Passwords or any value that is not a fixed-length code.

Instead:

- [Input](./input.md): Any other short value.

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] Screen readers hear one field with a label, and pasting the whole code works. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add input-otp
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Input otp reads 12 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Input otp's tokens to change Input otp alone.
